characterList.description: A young woman with long brown hair, wearing a blue scrub top. She is a Registered Nurse and the host of EmpowerRN!.
characterList.name: Caroline Potter Thomas

content_metadata.description: A video by EmpowerRN! featuring Caroline Potter Thomas exploring different needle sizes and colors used in nursing practice.

qAndA.question: What is the gauge and color of the smallest needle demonstrated?
What is the color of the needle most commonly used in adult medical-surgical units?

qAndA.answer: A filtered needle is used to prevent any broken glass fragments from being drawn into the syringe.
qAndA.question: What type of needle is used when drawing medication from a glass vial, and why?

qAndA.answer: She believes it offers a good balance between ease of use and providing a strong IV site.
qAndA.question: Why does Caroline personally favor the pink (20 gauge) needle?

qAndA.answer: The red needle is blunt and has a large bore hole, used for drawing and mixing medications.
qAndA.question: What type of needle has a blunt tip and a large bore hole?

youtube_description:
www.EmpoweRN.com

Hi Guys!
One thing that I thought was really interesting was that all of the needle sizes correlate with colors: at least in the U.S.
If you are from another country, please let me know if it is also the same!!
I also thought it was interesting that the larger the number... the smaller the needle.
For example: 
An 18 Gauge Needle is larger than a 25 Gauge Needle.
So I really hope that this video teaches, inspires & motivates you :)
If so, please give the video a "Thumbs Up" post a comment & subscribe to the channel!
I cannot wait to meet you!!
Much Love,
- Caroline Porter Thomas
